_about: Raw JSON-RPC exchange between the CloudDesk host's client (src/mcp_client.py) and Support Ops' ticket-history server over stdio, captured by experiments/week9_wire.py. Each 'raw' is byte-for-byte what crossed the pipe (one JSON object per line); 'annotations' explains every top-level field. The unannotated capture is week9/wire_raw.json.
_model_call: The model call happens only in the host (src/mcp_agent.py -> agent_runtime.chat): after step 5, when the model reads the discovered tools, and before step 6, when it chooses lookup_ticket and its arguments. It does not happen anywhere on this wire, in the client, or in the server: initialize, tools/list and tools/call are plain JSON-RPC answered by plain functions.
_transport: stdio: the host started the server as a child process (venv/bin/python third_party/ticket_history_server/server.py) and wrote each message as one line on its stdin; replies came back on its stdout, logs on its stderr. Over streamable HTTP the same messages are POSTed to one URL instead.

annotations.jsonrpc: Always the string "2.0": marks this as a JSON-RPC 2.0 message. MCP is JSON-RPC; nothing else on this wire.
annotations.id: 1. A request id chosen by the client. The reply must carry the same id; that is the only way a reply is matched to its request.
annotations.method: "initialize": the first message of every MCP session. Nothing else may be sent before it.
annotations.params: protocolVersion: the spec revision the client speaks (2025-06-18). capabilities: {} because this client offers the server nothing back (no sampling, no roots, no elicitation). clientInfo: who is calling, for the server's logs.

result.instructions: Support Ops ticket store. Ticket ids look like TCK-nnnn.

annotations.result: capabilities: what this server offers. tools, resources and prompts are all present, so the client may call tools/list, resources/list and prompts/list. listChanged false: it will not push notifications when its lists change. protocolVersion: the server agreed to 2025-06-18; had it not, the client would have to disconnect. serverInfo: name 'ticket-history', version left empty by Support Ops. instructions: free text the host may pass to its model; here it says ticket ids look like TCK-nnnn.

annotations.method: "notifications/initialized": the client confirms the handshake is done. It has no id because it is a notification: no reply comes back, and none is expected. Only after this is the session open for normal requests.
"tools/list": discovery. This answer, not the host's code, is where the agent's tool list comes from.
annotations.params: {}: no cursor, so the first page. The client follows nextCursor if the server pages; this server returned everything in one page.

tools.description:
Look up one support ticket by its id (format TCK-nnnn). Returns status,
    owner, subject, when it was opened, and how many times it was escalated.
    Does not return the escalation details; use get_escalation_history.
tools.name: lookup_ticket

tools.description:
Every escalation on one ticket (format TCK-nnnn), oldest first: when, from
    which team to which, who escalated it and why.
tools.name: get_escalation_history

annotations.result: tools: two definitions, lookup_ticket and get_escalation_history. Each has name (what the model will emit), description (the docstring, which is the prompt the model reads to decide whether to call it), and inputSchema (JSON Schema for the arguments; the host passes it to the model as the function's parameters). get_escalation_history also declares an outputSchema: its result has a typed shape. No nextCursor, so this is the whole list.

annotations.method: "tools/call": run one tool. In the agent, this message is built from the model's tool call: the model chose name and arguments, the client wrapped them in JSON-RPC.
annotations.params: name: "lookup_ticket", a name from step 5. arguments: {"ticket_id": "TCK-4471"}, which must validate against that tool's inputSchema.

content.text:
{
  "ticket_id": "TCK-4471",
  "customer_id": "CUS-371",
  "subject": "Priority customer: refund promised by previous shift",
  "status": "escalated",
  "owner": "tier2-meera",
  "opened_at": "2026-10-04T18:20:00Z",
  "escalation_count": 3
}

annotations.result: content: a list of content blocks; here one text block holding the ticket as JSON (status escalated, owner tier2-meera, 3 escalations). isError: false. A tool failure would come back here as isError true with the message in content, still a successful JSON-RPC result, so the model can read it and recover. A JSON-RPC error object is reserved for protocol failures such as an unknown method.
